title: Item effects
description: item_effects.yaml: what using each item does, as far as the executable says it: the function ITEM_FUNCTIONS names for it, HEALING_VALUES, EVOLUTION_ITEM_TARGET and the constants of the food and chip cases of handleFood and handleChips (formats/exe/item_effects.hpp). Status items, revives, battle disks and the special cases are logic the ruleset describes (rules/<id>/inventory.yaml).

item.description: The item's id in items.yaml; <pack id>:<name> for one a pack adds.

index.description: The item's index in ITEM_PARA; a row a pack adds for an item of its own has none.

handler.description: The function the item runs: none (NULL), hp_healing, mp_healing, double_floppy, status, revive (handleRestore), battle_disk (handleBuffDisks), chip, food or evolution.

healing.description: HP or MP healed (HEALING_VALUES), for hp_healing and mp_healing.

evolves_to.description: The Digimon an evolution item leads to (EVOLUTION_ITEM_TARGET): its id, or the raw number when outside DIGIMON_DATA; null outside that table's range.

values.description: The constants a food or chip case sets, by name; null for other handlers and for cases that do more than set them. Food has every key: energy, tiredness taken away, happiness, discipline, weight, lifetime in hours, max HP and MP added, HP and MP healed, offense, defense, speed and brains added, the training boost (setTrainingBoost: flag, value, hours) and the chance in 100 of getting sick. A chip has max_hp, max_mp, offense, defense, speed, brain and lifetime.
